title: The projection-normalized Tate derived augmentation is invertible
statement: Let $k$ be a field of positive prime characteristic different from the prime $\ell$ and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Choose normalized realization data $r$ [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization-records]. Put $R_X=p_X^*C(-,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ and $Z_X=\varprojlim_n\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ with root-power transitions [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. For $d\geq0$ put $P_d=Z_X^{\otimes_{R_X}d}$ with $P_0=R_X$, and form the strict positive finite tower $H_{n,d}$ using quotient and root-power maps. Encode it over the completed integral ring by the normalized coefficient equivalence [lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-comparison, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Then the morphism $P_d[0]\to R\varprojlim_n H_{n,d}[0]$ obtained by transposing the tensor projection cone through the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-pur-completed-rlim-functor] is an isomorphism. This is the actual morphism derivedAugmentation, with the specified projections and quotient unit at $d=0$.

proof.text: Use the normalized coefficient isomorphism to work over $R_X=A_X$. The actual finite quotient maps are unchanged.

source.place: Steps 2 and 4, integral reconstruction and coefficient transport

proof.text: Put $H_n=\mu_{\ell^n,X}$. It is killed by $\ell^n$ by [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. In the sheaf tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] define $a_n:R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H_n\to H_n$ by $r\otimes z\mapsto\rho_n(r)z$, with inverse $z\mapsto1\otimes z$. To check the other composite, locally lift $\rho_n(r)$ to an integer $a$ and write $r-a=\ell^n b$ locally using Step 1; then $(r-a)\otimes z=b\otimes\ell^n z=0$. These local identities prove the equality of sheaf maps. For the root-power map $t_n:H_{n+1}\to H_n$, one has $t_n(\rho_{n+1}(r)z)=\rho_n(r)t_n(z)$; hence $a_n(1\otimes t_n)=t_na_{n+1}$. At $n=0$, $H_0=\mu_{1,X}$ has only the identity section, so is the zero abelian sheaf and $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H_0=0$.

proof.text: The internal-module/section-ring equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] preserves the underlying sheaves. By the sectionwise limit construction [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], the compatible isomorphisms $a_n$ give $T_X\cong Z_X$ as $R$-modules. This also handles the index $0$ in [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]: a compatible family $(z_n)_{n\geq1}$ extends uniquely by $z_0=0$, and forgetting $z_0$ is its inverse. The comparison respects all positive-index projections, so the action of $R=\lim A_n$ on $Z_X$ is the one induced by the finite actions.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; sectionwise limits and the cone universal property

proof.text: For $d\geq0$ put $P_d=Z_X^{\otimes_R d}$, with $P_0=R$, and $H_{n,d}=H_n^{\otimes_{A_n}d}$, with $H_{n,0}=A_n$. Let $p_n:Z_X\to H_n$ be the limit projections; by Step 3 they are $R$-linear for the action of $R$ on $H_n$ through $\rho_n$, so $\varphi_n:Z_X\otimes_RA_n\to H_n$, $z\otimes\bar a\mapsto\bar a\,p_n(z)$, is well defined (balanced). Clause 1 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] makes the transitions $H_{n+1}\to H_n$ epimorphisms, so $p_n$ is an epimorphism by [det-pe-replete-epimorphism], and hence so is $\varphi_n$. Clause 2, with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its ring $\varprojlim_rA_r=R$ (Step 1), gives a pro-etale cover $\{V\}$ with $Z_X|_V\cong R|_V$, generated by a section $e$, and an abstract isomorphism $Z_X\otimes_RA_n\cong H_n$; restricted to $V$ both source and target of $\varphi_n$ are free of rank one over $A_n$. An $A_n$-linear epimorphism $A_n\to A_n$ is multiplication by a section $a$ with $1$ locally a multiple of $a$; so $a$ is locally, hence globally, a unit, and $\varphi_n|_V$ is an isomorphism. Thus $\varphi_n$ is an isomorphism and $p_n(e)$ generates $H_n|_V$. Tensoring the $\varphi_n$ gives $P_d\otimes_RA_n\to H_{n,d}$, $(z_1\otimes\cdots\otimes z_d)\otimes\bar a\mapsto\bar a\,p_n(z_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes p_n(z_d)$; on $V$ it sends the generator $e^{\otimes d}\otimes1$ to the generator $p_n(e)^{\otimes d}$, so it is an isomorphism. It commutes with transitions because $t_np_{n+1}=p_n$. Trivializing $H_{n,d}|_V$ by these compatible generators, the map $P_d\to\lim_nH_{n,d}$ becomes $R\to\lim_nA_n$ on $V$, an isomorphism by Step 1; restriction to $V$ commutes with these sectionwise limits, so $P_d\cong\lim_nH_{n,d}$ globally. The transitions $H_{n+1,d}\to H_{n,d}$ are epimorphisms: on $V$ they are the quotient maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. The positive-index tensor projections commute with these transitions by induction on d: at d=0 use the defining cokernel-map equation, and at a successor tensor the induction equality with the actual Tate-limit cone equation. Applying the integral encoding functor gives the naturality equation for the augmentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit], clauses 1-2, to the strict tower $(H_{n,d})_{n\geq1}$ of $R$-module sheaves; its epimorphism hypothesis was verified in Step 4. So $\lim_nH_{n,d}\cong P_d$ (Step 4) in degree zero, with the map to $\prod_nH_{n,d}$ given by the projections, is a derived limit: it has a Roos triangle on $1-s$, and $\prod_nH_{n,d}$ in degree zero is the product in $D(R)$. The functorial derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] has its natural Roos triangle on the same map $1-s$ of the same product. Applying (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to the rotated triangles with the identities of $\prod_nH_{n,d}$ gives $\psi:P_d\to R\lim_nH_{n,d}$ compatible with both maps to the product and with the connecting maps; by [lemma-weil-pbc-r-lim-levelwise-isomorphism] (all $u_n$ identities) $\psi$ is an isomorphism. It is the only morphism compatible with the projections: the difference of two such factors through a morphism $P_d\to(\prod_nH_{n,d})[-1]$, and the last clause of [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] says there is none but $0$ between sheaves placed in degrees $0$ and $1$. The exact functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] commutes with shifts, giving the required $R$-linear isomorphism $M_d\cong P_d[2d]$, determined by the compatible projections $P_d\to H_{n,d}$.
